reason: os_free(eloop.readers) inside eloop_destroy(); 'eloop' is a file-scope static struct with no initializer, so the C standard guarantees it is zero-initialized before any code runs, meaning eloop.readers is NULL even if eloop_init() were somehow skipped. os_free maps to free(), which is a defined no-op on NULL, and every real caller (hostapd/main.c, wpa_supplicant.c, eapol_test.c, wpa_cli.c, etc.) invokes eloop_init() once before eloop_destroy() and destroys only once per process, so no path reads a genuinely indeterminate value or double-frees a stale pointer. The rule is treating implicit static zero-init as if it were uninitialized memory.
